items.title: Dual proofs of legendary Riemann hypothesis stun mathematicians
items.summary: Experts say the AI and human-written proofs will need careful checking — plus, the fallout from the COP31 climate conference.

items.title: ‘If we can solve Riemann, what can’t we do?’: mathematicians shocked and excited by AI breakthroughs
items.summary: Awe, anxiety and opportunity: mathematics community shares mixed emotions following the solution of the field’s biggest unsolved problem.

items.title: Has AI just cracked Internet encryption? Rumoured ‘bombshell’ stuns scientists
items.summary: AI-generated algorithms could be about to break public-key cryptography, the technology central to commerce, banking and privacy.

items.title: Daily briefing: A guide to the Riemann hypothesis
items.summary: Get to grips with the famed conjecture, and hear mathematicians’ reactions to its proofs. Plus, the benefits of eating with other people.

items.title: An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage
items.summary: Reconstruction of radiative forcing resulting from worldwide peatland drainage over the past two centuries reveals a persistent net warming effect caused by the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO2 emissions over that of avoided CH4 emissions.

items.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis? A guide to the famed conjecture that rules prime numbers
items.summary: The biggest problem in mathematics has to do with a statistical test familiar to scientists.

items.title: Life-saving cancer drug pumped out by a plant
items.summary: In a proof-of-concept study, scientists have coaxed a tobacco-related plant to synthesize the chemotherapy drug paclitaxel.

items.title: Why the incoming US Congress should ban the development of self-improving AI
items.summary: Voters are demanding greater control over this new technology. Political leaders must respond by keeping humans in charge of AI development.

items.title: A powerful HIV vaccine is finally within reach — thanks to these super antibodies
items.summary: Potent immune responses against diverse HIV strains have ignited the field, but major hurdles remain.

items.title: Brain area’s mysterious role in speech decoded at last
items.summary: Wernicke’s area is known for processing spoken words, but brain recordings reveal that it also makes a crucial contribution to a related cognitive task.

items.title: Orangutans face bleak future after Indonesia’s devastating wildfires
items.summary: The super El Niño intensified Indonesian fires, which ravaged the habitat of the critically endangered Bornean orangutan.

items.title: Dengue has exploded globally with shocking speed
items.summary: The number of recorded cases of the mosquito-borne disease worldwide rose by a factor of 34 over 34 years.

items.title: Licensing mechanisms during RNA-guided DNA integration by type I-F3 CAST
items.summary: RNA-guided DNA integration by type I-F3 CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs) is enhanced by redesigned TnsA and a holo complex whose coordinated conformational licensing reveals a conserved mechanistic framework for engineering highly active CASTs.

items.title: Sustainable cement production via a liquid-phase pathway
items.summary: Sustainable cement production can be achieved by accelerating its reaction kinetics through a microwave carbon-plasma method, reducing the standard processing time from hours to seconds.

items.title: Chromosome ‘glue’ could boost fertility by stabilizing ageing eggs
items.summary: A system tested in mice mimics a protein that declines with age and could help to improve fertility treatments in future.

items.title: An in situ redox-converted molecule for all-perovskite tandem solar cells
items.summary: An in situ redox-converted molecule for all-perovskite tandem solar cells

items.title: Bogong moths can migrate using an internal geomagnetic compass
items.summary: Australian migratory moths navigate long distances, in part owing to a stellar ‘compass’. It transpires that they have another compass that detects the inclination, or angle, of Earth’s magnetic field lines and that probably relies on a light-dependent quantum-mechanical mechanism similar to the one found in night-migratory songbirds.

items.title: Rare gene variants can affect a person’s height by up to 17 centimetres
items.summary: An analysis of 1.4 million people uncovered rare gene variants that are helping to unpick the genetic architecture behind the heritability of height.

items.title: Gut microbes can adapt to our ageing bodies
items.summary: A study of more than 10,000 individuals reveals specific mutations in gut bacteria that arise during human ageing, but few mutations associated with disease.

items.title: Pockets in compacted DNA tune gene activation
items.summary: The stochastic activation of specific genes is needed for the proper formation of neuronal circuits. Opposing forces act on inactive DNA to balance this process.

items.title: A fine-grained reconstruction of barley’s evolutionary history
items.summary: Chromosome-scale genome sequences from across the barley genus Hordeum reveal large structural variation, evidence of ancient genetic exchange and extensive divergence of regulatory sequences. These evolutionary processes have generated diversity that could be used to improve cultivated barley.

items.title: The world has a golden chance to improve HIV prevention: don’t squander it
items.summary: Generic versions of an effective HIV drug have been approved, and an HIV vaccine is on the horizon. Now is no time for funders to take their foot off the pedal.

items.title: Enzymatic reactions adapted to make ‘living’ chains of sugars
items.summary: By tuning the binding between enzymes that chain sugars together and the molecules that initiate the reaction, precise chain lengths have been made for biological studies.

items.title: Single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map for coronary artery disease
items.summary: A multi-omic gene-expression and chromatin-accessibility map of human coronary artery disease provides a framework for mapping disease-associated genetic variants to cell types, chromatin states and gene programmes in human disease.

items.title: Heterogeneity co-evolves with architecture to determine colon cancer outcome
items.summary: Architectural interfaces in colorectal cancer drive cell state diversification through mechanochemical reprogramming of stem cell identities.

items.title: A gut–brain sensory-motor circuit regulates sugar ingestion in Drosophila
items.summary: In flies, sugar-sensing enteric neurons activate brain neurons that inhibit crop duct motor neurons, relaxing the foregut muscles to facilitate food transfer to the crop, which sustains ingestion and regulates food intake.

items.title: Quantum-enhanced sensing with 500 photons via Fock-space confocal focusing
items.summary: Quantum confocal microscopy enables deterministic preparation of high-photon-number Fock-like states with up to 500 photons, reducing photon-number variance by 21.5 dB and achieving record displacement-sensing precision 19.2 dB beyond the standard quantum limit.

items.title: Enzymatic living polymerization for polysaccharide synthesis
items.summary: An enzymatic method for making high-molecular-weight polysaccharides in a way similar to synthetic polymerization techniques, rather than biosynthetically, is presented.

items.title: How arteries keep their shape in the face of overgrowth-inducing mutations
items.summary: Why do cancer-associated mutations cause some blood vessels to develop abnormally, but not arteries? The answer lies in the identity and maturity of the affected cells.

items.title: From sketch to publication-ready flowchart: how AI tools can bridge the gap
items.summary: The use of generative AI is a practical way to translate hand-drawn scientific diagrams into digital formats without handing over total control, explains Ensar Aydemir.

items.title: Middle–Late Pleistocene Denisovans and unresolved Homo in southern China
items.summary: Dental morphology and proteomic analyses of fossils from southern China identify lineages with and without Denisovan affinity, indicating the diversity of hominin populations in this region in the Middle to Late Pleistocene.

items.title: Augmenting reality with integrated photonics
items.summary: Integrated photonics could overcome key size, power and performance trade-offs in augmented-reality glasses, enabling compact, efficient displays while opening opportunities across quantum computing, bioimaging and optical sensing.

items.title: How Singapore has turned a nation into a smart-city testing ground
items.summary: The city-state’s compact size and centralized governance allow digital infrastructure to be introduced with unusual speed and consistency.

items.title: Can Beijing scale up its smart-city ambitions?
items.summary: The world’s leading science city is testing AI and intelligent transport at scale, but linking data across its innovation hubs remains a challenge.

items.title: China’s AI-powered smart-city model is going global
items.summary: China is using AI and big data to connect its cities and rural regions. Now, its smart-city technologies are attracting international interest.

items.title: Helsinki puts trust at the heart of its smart-city model
items.summary: Open urban data, recycled data-centre heat and a public AI register are helping the Finnish capital develop responsible urban technology.

items.title: Context-dependent response of endothelial cells to PIK3CA mutation
items.summary: Expression of PIK3CAH1047R in arterial precursors disrupts arterial differentiation and promotes the acquisition of venous features.

items.title: The haunting loveliness of boglands: Books in brief
items.summary: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

items.title: The leading cities in the world for high-quality research in 2025
items.summary: A decade of data on the top-performing science cities in the Nature Index.

items.title: Saving Nepal’s wild orchids — in photos
items.summary: Prized for their ornamental and medicinal value, hundreds of orchids are illegally harvested and sold each year. Now, conservationist Reshu Bashyal is leading an effort to protect them.

items.title: The world’s leading science cities are changing — here’s why
items.summary: Nature Index data reveal the cities that are gaining ground in research, as smart technologies transform how urban centres operate and compete for talent.

items.title: London’s people-first approach to smart-city development
items.summary: Digital twins and open-data platforms are part of London’s aim to innovate for citizens.

items.title: Can smart cities attract the talent they need to thrive?
items.summary: The challenges of high-tech cities in South Korea and China reveal what scientists really want.

items.title: Succumbing to certainty is a failure in science
items.summary: Researchers can face pressure from policymakers and politicians to provide single, definitive answers to complex challenges. They should resist, says Andy Stirling.

items.title: Just eight universities dominate Nobel and other top economics prizes
items.summary: Economics is the outlier — top prizes in science, engineering and other social sciences go to researchers at a greater variety of institutions.

items.title: Postcards from your graves
items.summary: A disastrous outcome.

items.title: Navigating grief in academia: ways to find balance
items.summary: Pamela Yeh found it hard to manage grief and the demands of her work. Here are some steps that helped her to ease the burden.
